findings.what: The States row "`/`, no items" (200, list hidden, filter links shown with All current, "No items yet.", Go back hidden) only has the old test "says so when the table is empty", which checks the message and nothing else. No test checks that the filter links (with All current) still show on an empty table, or that no list or Go back appears. More broadly, no 200-state test asserts that "Go back" is hidden.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, assert currentLinks(html) equals ["All"], that there is no <li>, and that there is no id="back". Add a not.toContain('id="back"') assertion to the AC-3/AC-5/AC-6 tests too.

findings.what: The Go back script requires `history.length > 1` as well as a same-origin referrer. The spec's decision says to go back whenever document.referrer is same-origin, and it names history.length > 1 only as a rejected approach. The extra guard is arguably safer (a link opened in a new tab has a same-origin referrer but no history), but the spec doesn't record it.
findings.fix: Either drop the `history.length > 1` condition to match the decision as written, or record the extra guard in the spec's Go back decision.

findings.what: items.category_id has a REFERENCES constraint. SQLite refuses `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` on a column used in a foreign key, so the mechanical reverse in scripts/schema.mjs (used by scripts/reset-to-baseline.sh) is expected to fail its self-check (exit 3) the next time this repo is reset to baseline-3. A hand-written reset migration would then be needed. The spec doesn't mention this. I couldn't run it here.
findings.fix: Confirm by running `node scripts/schema.mjs reverse` against baseline-3. If it fails, either record in the spec that the next reset needs a hand-written migration, or teach schema.mjs to rebuild the table instead of dropping a foreign-key column.
